question_text: What is the primary purpose of a GPU?
correct_answer: Perform highly parallel computations

question_text: What is a major architectural difference between a typical CPU and GPU?
options: GPUs generally contain many more parallel execution resources
correct_answer: GPUs generally contain many more parallel execution resources

question_text: GPUs are particularly well suited for which type of workload?
correct_answer: Highly parallel workloads

question_text: What is a GPU streaming multiprocessor generally responsible for?
options: Executing groups of GPU threads and managing their resources
correct_answer: Executing groups of GPU threads and managing their resources

question_text: What is a GPU thread?
options: An individual execution instance of a GPU kernel
correct_answer: An individual execution instance of a GPU kernel

question_text: What is a GPU kernel?
options: A function executed by many GPU threads in parallel
The physical center of a GPU chip
correct_answer: A function executed by many GPU threads in parallel

question_text: What is CUDA?
options: A parallel computing platform and programming model for NVIDIA GPUs
correct_answer: A parallel computing platform and programming model for NVIDIA GPUs

question_text: What is VRAM primarily used for?
options: Store graphics data and other data accessed by the GPU
correct_answer: Store graphics data and other data accessed by the GPU

question_text: Which stage of a traditional graphics pipeline converts geometric primitives into fragments?
correct_answer: Rasterization

question_text: What is a shader?
options: A program executed on the GPU to perform graphics or compute operations
correct_answer: A program executed on the GPU to perform graphics or compute operations

question_text: What does a vertex shader primarily operate on?
correct_answer: Vertices

question_text: What does a fragment shader primarily determine?
options: The color and other properties of fragments or pixels
correct_answer: The color and other properties of fragments or pixels

question_text: Which of the following is a graphics API commonly used to communicate with GPUs?
correct_answer: Vulkan

question_text: What is OpenGL primarily used for?
correct_answer: Rendering 2D and 3D graphics

question_text: What is GPGPU computing?
options: Using GPUs for general-purpose computations beyond graphics
Using GPUs only for displaying images
correct_answer: Using GPUs for general-purpose computations beyond graphics

question_text: In CUDA, what is a thread block?
options: A group of threads that can cooperate and share certain resources
correct_answer: A group of threads that can cooperate and share certain resources

question_text: In CUDA, what is a grid?
options: The collection of thread blocks launched for a kernel
correct_answer: The collection of thread blocks launched for a kernel

question_text: Which type of GPU memory is typically private to an individual thread?
correct_answer: Local memory

question_text: Which GPU memory is typically accessible by threads across the device and has relatively high capacity?
correct_answer: Global memory

question_text: What is shared memory in CUDA primarily used for?
options: Fast data sharing among threads in the same block
correct_answer: Fast data sharing among threads in the same block

question_text: Why are GPU registers important for performance?
options: They provide very fast storage for values used by individual threads
correct_answer: They provide very fast storage for values used by individual threads

question_text: What is coalesced memory access in GPU programming?
options: Efficiently combining nearby thread memory accesses into fewer memory transactions
Copying all GPU memory to the CPU
correct_answer: Efficiently combining nearby thread memory accesses into fewer memory transactions

question_text: What does SIMT stand for?
correct_answer: Single Instruction, Multiple Threads

question_text: What is a warp in NVIDIA CUDA terminology?
options: A group of threads scheduled and executed together
correct_answer: A group of threads scheduled and executed together

question_text: What is GPU occupancy?
options: The ratio of active warps to the maximum supported active warps on a compute unit
The percentage of VRAM that is permanently reserved
correct_answer: The ratio of active warps to the maximum supported active warps on a compute unit

question_text: Why is matrix multiplication well suited to GPU execution?
options: Many matrix elements can be computed independently in parallel
correct_answer: Many matrix elements can be computed independently in parallel

question_text: What is a framebuffer?
options: A memory region containing data used to represent an image for display
correct_answer: A memory region containing data used to represent an image for display

question_text: What is depth buffering used for in 3D graphics?
options: Determine which surfaces are visible based on depth
correct_answer: Determine which surfaces are visible based on depth

question_text: What is rasterization?
options: Converting geometric primitives into fragments or pixels for rendering
Converting source code into machine code
correct_answer: Converting geometric primitives into fragments or pixels for rendering

question_text: What is texture mapping used for?
options: Apply image or texture data to surfaces in a rendered scene
correct_answer: Apply image or texture data to surfaces in a rendered scene

question_text: What is a GPU memory bank conflict?
options: When threads in a warp access different addresses that map to the same shared-memory bank
When two shaders have the same name
correct_answer: When threads in a warp access different addresses that map to the same shared-memory bank

question_text: What is warp divergence?
options: When threads in the same warp take different control-flow paths
When all threads execute identical instructions
When a GPU changes its display resolution
correct_answer: When threads in the same warp take different control-flow paths

question_text: Why can excessive register usage reduce GPU occupancy?
options: More registers per thread can limit how many threads or warps fit on a compute unit
Registers are stored only on the CPU
correct_answer: More registers per thread can limit how many threads or warps fit on a compute unit

question_text: What is the main purpose of a GPU's memory hierarchy?
options: Provide different storage levels that balance latency, capacity, bandwidth, and access patterns
correct_answer: Provide different storage levels that balance latency, capacity, bandwidth, and access patterns

question_text: What is a tensor core primarily designed to accelerate?
options: Matrix and tensor operations used heavily in machine learning
correct_answer: Matrix and tensor operations used heavily in machine learning

question_text: What is the primary difference between a GPU execution unit and a CPU core?
options: GPU execution resources are generally optimized for high throughput across many parallel threads
GPU execution units cannot perform arithmetic
correct_answer: GPU execution resources are generally optimized for high throughput across many parallel threads

question_text: Why are high-bandwidth GPU interconnects important in multi-GPU systems?
options: They enable faster communication and data exchange between GPUs
They eliminate the need for kernels
correct_answer: They enable faster communication and data exchange between GPUs

question_text: What is the purpose of hardware ray-tracing acceleration in modern GPUs?
options: Accelerate calculations for ray-object intersections and related ray-tracing operations
correct_answer: Accelerate calculations for ray-object intersections and related ray-tracing operations

question_text: What is the role of a GPU warp scheduler?
options: Select eligible warps for execution on available execution resources
correct_answer: Select eligible warps for execution on available execution resources

question_text: What does GPU throughput measure?
options: The amount of computation or work the GPU can complete per unit of time
The physical size of the GPU
The amount of disk space available
correct_answer: The amount of computation or work the GPU can complete per unit of time
